floor_history.headline: recon s1: floor 64 -> 36 pure C; epilogue+prologue matched; residual = inner-loop back-edge delay slot (label between increments and inner++) + seat cascade; counter/biv-elimination and hit-after-loop

frontier.hypothesis: An ordinary-C spelling exists whose RTL has the hit block out of line while the increments fall straight into inner++ (no label/jump between), which lets reorg fill the back-edge slot with `acc += step` as in the target
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c:2969 fill_simple_delay_slots stops at CODE_LABEL; the relocation mechanism seen on v11's scan block (fresh label after a barrier) is the likely source of the target's out-of-line hit block
frontier.next_probe: Instrumented cc1 with BB2_XJUMP_DEBUG=1 on v11 vs v13 to name the pass that minted label 262; then measure (a) v13 with the hit arm first, (b) v3 shape with break + foldable post-loop test, (c) do/while inner loop, (d) increments in the for-clause with continue; pairdiff + .dbr dump each

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining seat cascade (pitch $a3->$a0, bit/shift/curve/lower/outer/acc/step) is a consequence of the structural residual and the pseudo set, not an independent RA lock
frontier.mechanism: global.c priority order and conflict sets change once the then-arm jump/label disappear and `inner` takes $a0
frontier.next_probe: After F1 lands, run tools/ra_solver inverse_compose.py classify on the v13-derived form before spelling any seat lever

frontier.hypothesis: If F1 has no ordinary spelling, the two-pass reorg route (make the loop-top peel ineligible on pass 1 so pass 2 sees the deleted `j Lend`) reproduces the slot
frontier.mechanism: dbr_schedule runs MAX_REORG_PASSES; relax_delay_slots deletes the jump-to-next after the hit block is stolen
frontier.next_probe: Read v13's .dbr dump for the first-pass fill order; low priority
